memoryRule: a completed page turn shuts the seen fold, invents an opening in a non-local unread fold, and echoes the crease in a third fold; later turns inherit the false pagination
interactionRule: wheel, swipe, or arrow-key page turns are geometry-neutral while shallow; a full turn commits; Delete lifts latest; Escape or R releases
representationRupture: Canvas pressure plate, WebGL relief, and Canvas proof sheet -> one browser-native DOM/CSS accordion page made from overlapping folds
compositionRupture: singular negative plate, faceted relief, and typographic register -> a crooked diagonal page with an open interval and overlapping leaves
encounterRupture: draw a pressure stroke, hold a look, or compose a witness -> scroll, swipe, or turn a page through an accumulated reading threshold
temporalRupture: pressure inference, false reconstruction, and proof mishearing -> false pagination in which the unseen page answers and the wrong crease persists
mediumRupture: p5.js Canvas 2D/WebGL and raster geometry -> semantic browser DOM with CSS clip-path, transform, and actual fold geometry; no canvas or SVG renderer
changedRule: The reader's completed turn is treated as evidence, but the page misreads it: the visible fold shuts, an unseen fold invents an opening, and a third fold echoes the crease in the wrong direction.
visibleConsequence: A blind crooked accordion page becomes materially re-paginated after a full turn: the focused leaf narrows, a remote leaf grows and moves, and a third leaf changes its crease; four errors remain visible.
falsifier: Delete if the first view reads as a card grid, if scrolling is decorative, if the seen leaf alone answers, if remote opening or echoed crease is cosmetic, if later turns reset, or if exact lifting fails.
deletionCondition: Delete v036 if caption-free viewing cannot distinguish the false accordion from the prior plate, relief, and proof grammars, or if page turns change only colour, labels, or readout.
promotion: candidate / held pending local and production browser matrices, independent caption-free perceptual review, and provider revision linkage
